messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: high-5xx-rate on /v1/generate (region: us-west-2). P95 latency > 3s. Auto-paging to oncall group.
Ashley: I’m on it — paging into triage. Customer reports increased failures and slow responses since ~10:12 UTC.
Mike: I’m seeing a sudden drop in KV prefix hit-rate for model kv-store: went from ~98% -> ~60% at ~10:11.
Sara: Confirmed. Dashboards show prefix eviction spikes around the same time. Any deploys?
Ben: No user-facing deploys in last hour. infra did push a config change to redis cluster TTLs at 10:05 — rolling restart completed by 10:09.
Nick: That aligns. TTL config change might have triggered mass invalidation if keys were migrated.
Ashley: Impact assessment: several mid-sized customers reported 5xxs and timeouts for generation. Most errors are 504/503 gateway timeouts and a small portion 500 from runtime.
Mike: Logs (sampling) show model runtime errors due to cache miss storm and increased load to origin:
```
[10:12:31] INFO prefix_lookup miss key=prefix_0x1a user=acct-123
[10:12:31] WARN kv_fetch latency=120ms backend=store-east
[10:12:32] ERROR runtime queue_depth=254 target_latency_exceeded
```
Sara: We’re seeing continuous rewarm attempts that thrash the KV layer — lots of parallel re-fetches. No graceful backoff.
Ben: ops-bot, can you dump recent eviction log from redis cluster and share top prefixes?
ops-bot: Attached eviction-summary (last 30m): top evicted prefixes = ["pref_A", "pref_B", "pref_C"], eviction-rate spike at 10:10 -> 10:14.
Ashley: Hypothesis 1: TTL config rollback/reshard caused key TTL reset or migration, leading to large-scale invalidations -> cache miss storm -> origin overload -> runtime timeouts.
Mike: Hypothesis 2: A change to prefix hashing (rare) could have altered key namespace mapping causing cache misses across nodes. I’ll check commit history.
Nick: Hypothesis 3: Autoscaler reacted to increased load but scaled down cache capacity briefly due to metric mis-eval. Check scaling logs.
Ben: I’m pulling the deployment and config events: redis-ttl-update #PR-842 merged at 10:04, applied via k8s rolling restart 10:06-10:09. No hashing changes in that PR.
Sara: Reproduction: in staging, applying the same TTL update produced no mass invalidation — keyspace was preserved. Difference: production had a reshard step due to node replacement that occurred right before restart. Possible race.
Ashley: Immediate mitigations in-flight: 1) Pause client retries at edge for affected routes (to avoid origin storm). 2) Temporarily route a subset of traffic to dedicated capacity (reduces pressure). 3) Increase cache retention window / disable eviction for top prefixes. 4) Rolling back TTL change if we confirm it's causal.
Mike: Implemented edge rate-limiter for /v1/generate -> reduced new origin requests by ~40%. Slow drop in 5xxs observed after 10:25.
Ben: I initiated TTL rollback at 10:28 and set redis nodes to restore previous slot assignments; rollback finished 10:33.
Nick: After rollback, prefix hit-rate climbed from 62% -> ~90% over ~7 minutes for top keys. Warmup is ongoing.
Ashley: Customer impact note: Affected customers had higher latency and transient 5xxs between 10:11–10:30. Post-mitigation, some requests still slower until KV rewarm finished (~10:45). No data loss.
Sara: Collecting timeline artifacts: redis logs, k8s rollout events, eviction-summary, origin request graphs, and sample runtime error traces. Dropping links in thread.
Ben: Sharing logs (truncated):
```
-- redis node 3 --
10:08:52 FAILOVER start migrating slots
10:09:01 migrating 16384 slots -> node-7
10:09:10 restart triggered
10:10:11 eviction spike: incr 1800/min
```
Mike: Runtime trace (snippet):
```
10:12:30 request id=abc123 prefix_miss=true rewarm_spawned=12
10:12:31 queue_depth=240 worker_timeouts=3
```
Nick: For next actions: 1) Full RCA doc — timeline + root cause. 2) Add guardrails to prevent reshard + TTL-change combo. 3) Instrument KV rewarm backoff and request dedupe. 4) Run a small-scale chaos test to validate behavior.
Ashley: Assigning owners: RCA doc -> Mike, Kv-guardrail proposals -> Ben, Instrumentation work -> Sara, Postmortem coordination -> Ashley.
ops-bot: Incident severity updated -> sev2 (customer-impacting).
Mike: Early conclusion: root cause likely an overlap of node reshard (slot movement) and TTL config roll leading to transient key unavailability and mass invalidation. The mass re-fetch without request-level backoff produced origin overload and runtime queue saturation.
Ashley: Will produce a short customer-facing summary for CSMs by EOD. If anyone sees lingering regressions, ping here. :thumbsup:
Ben: Adding a quick mitigation: pre-warm top N prefixes after any slot migration or restart. I’ll draft a runbook.
Sara: Noting a follow-up: add adaptive client-side jitter to reduce simultaneous rewarm.
Mike: I’ll publish the timeline artifact and logs to the incident storage bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1929812345/. Link: https://s3.console.aws/#/bucket/redwood-incidents/1929812345
Ashley: Thanks team. Handoff to post-incident RCA channel in 30m.
ops-bot: Incident closed to active paging at 11:05."
